Hi @RorryB , thanks for the report!

From how the hooks are implemented the expected ordering is [`automatic_optimization.run (training_step + optimizer.step)`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/862314360457fed35672ec9d0c6f5f1998a61eae/src/lightning/pytorch/loops/training_epoch_loop.py#L240) -> [`on_validation_epoch_end`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/862314360457fed35672ec9d0c6f5f1998a61eae/src/lightning/pytorch/loops/training_epoch_loop.py#L285). Could you share a bit more about whats not working for you or what behavior you expect instead?

Sure, so I would expect the ordering to be

comments.author: GdoongMathew
comments.body:
Thanks for the clarification. So this is actually an expected behavior caused by `lightning` utilizing the closure mechanism in torch optimizer. A reference could be found in this https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/pull/21120#issuecomment-3227587883 as well.

Basically, `lightning` wraps the work from `training_step` through `on_before_optimizer_step` into one big closure function and passes that to `optimizer.step` argument. Optimizer would call that closure internally ([ref](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/optim/sgd.py#L114-L116)). That's why the logs can look like `optimizer.step` runs before `training_step`, but the training logic inside the closure is still executed before the actual parameter update.

comments.author: GdoongMathew
comments.body:
So, at a high level, the pseudo-code for the optimizer closure looks like this:

```python
def closure():
    LightningModule.training_step()
    LightningModule.optimizer_zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    LightningModule.on_before_optimizer_step()

optimizer.step(closure=closure)
```

If you add a debug print before and after the `optimizer.step`

```python
class LightningMNISTClassifier(pl.LightningModule):
    def optimizer_step(self, epoch, batch_idx, optimizer, optimizer_closure):
        print(f"DEBUG: optimizer_step called (epoch {epoch}, batch {batch_idx})", flush=True)
        optimizer.step(closure=optimizer_closure)    # --> The `training_step` is included in the `optimizer_closure` here
        print(f"DEBUG: optimizer_step called finished (epoch {epoch}, batch {batch_idx})", flush=True)
```

Then you should see logs similar to the following:
```text
DEBUG: optimizer_step called (epoch 0, batch 858)
DEBUG: training_step start (batch 858)
DEBUG: training_step end (batch 858)
DEBUG: optimizer_step called finished (epoch 0, batch 858)
```
 which shows the training step is executed within the optimizer step via the provided closure, rather than being called separately afterward.

comments.author: RorryB
comments.body:
Awesome, thank you for this detailed explanation!  This helped me track down my bug.  I've never seen this step(closure) idea before.  

FYI, and If anyone else looks at this later with the same problem, I have fairly complicated setup for my project that does some other stuff before the step().  My usual order without Lightning is training step -> zero grad -> other stuff -> optimizer step.  But closure was re ordering it to be other stuff -> training step -> zero grad -> optimizer step.  By taking this closure concept into account I was able to rearrange where my other stuff is running and get things in the right order.

Thanks again!
